critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 921 lines and index.tsx is 779 lines — both above the 700-line soft cap. Consider splitting server.py into routers (auth, engagements, milestones, public, payments, pdf, attachments) and extracting screens/components (Dashboard, EngagementView, EditMilestonePanel, PDF button) from index.tsx.
server.py still uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') — migrate to lifespan handler (carried from iter 4/5).

_require_pre_scope() returns 409 for both 'active' and 'archived' with the same message 'Checkpoints can only be edited before the client accepts scope' — misleading when engagement is archived; consider branching the message based on doc['status'].

PDF endpoint /api/public/engagements/{token}/summary.pdf is unauthenticated — anyone with the share token gets the full financial breakdown including fees, expenses, and total. If share tokens are meant to be shareable-but-guessable, this may leak revenue data. Consider rate-limiting or requiring auth for archived engagements.

Receipt email is fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task with no retry/DLQ path; if the Emergent email proxy 429s or fails, the client never receives the receipt and there's no operator visibility. Consider logging failures to a collection or using the same reminder-loop pattern as payments.

unarchive_engagement() decides new_status purely from scope_accepted_at presence — a previously 'archived from awaiting_scope_acceptance' that later has scope_accepted_at somehow set would go straight to 'active' (currently impossible but a subtle invariant to preserve).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (5/5 flows: milestone edit, add, archive+dashboard toggle+restore, client-archived notice, client-active read-only)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL from /app/frontend/.env: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://checkpoint-app-10.preview.emergentagent.com. Run backend suite with `python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v -o addopts=` (pytest.ini enables xdist which breaks the module-scoped fixtures — force sequential). Receipt email test uses `caplog` for in-process log capture, NOT supervisor log — problem statement's '/var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log Receipt:' assertion is impossible because _mark_paid is called from the pytest process, so logger.info writes to pytest stdout instead. Emergent email proxy occasionally returns 429; treated as evidence of a real send attempt.
